cases.reason: GR16d defers to §2002:14.5.12.1.3, whose rule 2 continues the statement only if the declarative 'completes normally', and §2002:14.5.12.1.1 rule 1 makes EXIT FUNCTION and EXIT METHOD in the declarative an abnormal completion. 2023's list (§2023:14.6.13.1.2) has neither, because 2023 removed both statements (§2023:E.2). So the 2002 scope includes an UNSTRING overflow in a method or function whose EC-OVERFLOW-UNSTRING declarative executes EXIT METHOD / EXIT FUNCTION: the UNSTRING does not continue, NOT ON OVERFLOW is not run. No 2023 test can contain that program (EXIT METHOD is refused at --std 2023, COBOL0902). The compiler is correct at 2002 (probe r5: M-START / DECL / CALLER-BACK), so the row needs its own 2002 witness, not a carried 2023 verdict.

cases.reason: GR12 is defined over the I-O status value. In 2002 that domain includes status 38 (OPEN on a connector closed WITH LOCK), which 2023 removed together with CLOSE WITH LOCK (§2023:E.2). So a 2002 program exists whose format 3 EC-I-O declarative runs for a fatal 38, and no 2023 test can contain it (CLOSE WITH LOCK is refused at 2023, COBOL0902). The handling is the generic fatal 3x path, and the compiler is correct at 2002 (probe r7: USE-EC 38, then abnormal termination EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR). Separately I checked the EC-I-O-WARNING (2023-only) case: at 2002 a status 05 OPEN does not run the declarative (probe r1, correct). To settle it, decide whether a 2002-only status value that a removed phrase produces counts as part of this status-driven rule's scope. If it does, the row is OVERTURNED (class other) with r7 as its witness.

cases.reason: GR13 selects the format 4 declarative for 'the exception object that was raised'. In 2002 an exception object can also be raised into the activating element by EXIT METHOD RAISING identifier-1 or EXIT FUNCTION RAISING identifier-1 (§2002:14.8.13.3 GR3b, then §2002:14.5.12.1.4 rule 2: the activating element's USE selects). 2023 has neither statement (§2023:E.2; 2023 14.9.14 has no method or function format), so the 2023 row's witnesses cannot contain that program, and the compiler refuses it at --std 2023 (COBOL0902). The compiler is correct at 2002: probe r3 (EXIT METHOD RAISING M1 into the caller's USE AFTER EO R3ERR) prints CALLER-START / M-BEFORE / EO-CAUGHT-EQ / AFTER-INVOKE / END. This is a reach to a removed statement form through the rule's input, not through its own clause's format.
